name: 夫が妻の姓を選ぶとき、それぞれの声

p_28aea2d27e.sentence: I was grateful that both sets of parents accepted my decision without taking offense.
p_28aea2d27e.prev: It was my wife’s parents who worried, asking me again and again if I was really sure.
p_28aea2d27e.next: I still find it a little hard that I don’t get much time to myself while living at my wife’s parents’ home, but adjusting to the way each family does things was harder than changing my last name.

p_c9477d3e1a.sentence: I need to let go of my son, don’t I?
p_c9477d3e1a.prev: Someone told me that was an old-fashioned way to think, and I think they were right.
p_c9477d3e1a.next: I still feel sad, but I want to accept his choice to take his wife’s last name.

p_bb5820f386.sentence: Even so, I don’t want to hold my son back because of my feelings as a parent.
p_bb5820f386.prev: I say that they should decide for themselves, but that still bothers me.
p_bb5820f386.next: If he talked to me before deciding on a last name, I could share how I feel, too.

p_224027b3ab.sentence: In a conversation about last names, perhaps a person’s own choice overlaps with the feeling that a parent is giving something up.
p_224027b3ab.prev: A parent who respects a son’s choice said they wanted the other parents to feel at least a little grateful to their son.
p_224027b3ab.next: Alongside the couple’s decision about their last name, there are feelings that parents want to share with the other parents.

p_d4ec010f33.sentence: When they care about different things, how can they choose something they can both accept?
p_d4ec010f33.prev: Whether a husband chooses his wife’s last name on the marriage registration form or joins her family as an adopted son, he and each of their families have their own feelings.
p_d4ec010f33.next: Here are the voices of three people with different situations and lives.

p_f2efadbdd6.sentence: I still find it a little hard that I don’t get much time to myself while living at my wife’s parents’ home, but adjusting to the way each family does things was harder than changing my last name.
p_f2efadbdd6.prev: I was grateful that both sets of parents accepted my decision without taking offense.
p_f2efadbdd6.next: Once I could accept that of course we were different, I felt much more at ease.

p_6337623c8d.sentence: When he said he would change his last name too, I felt like my son was moving away, and I got very upset.
p_6337623c8d.prev: He’ll live near her parents’ home, far from us.
p_6337623c8d.next: But was it only the change of last name that I didn’t like?

p_07ed712929.sentence: Once I could accept that of course we were different, I felt much more at ease.
p_07ed712929.prev: I still find it a little hard that I don’t get much time to myself while living at my wife’s parents’ home, but adjusting to the way each family does things was harder than changing my last name.
p_07ed712929.next: The next speaker is a mother whose son is getting married next year.

p_b2d72d0085.sentence: I had no problem at all with changing my last name.
p_b2d72d0085.prev: I became an adopted son in my wife’s family and took their last name.
p_b2d72d0085.next: My parents accepted it easily, even though my hometown is way out in the country.

p_be39c95a7f.sentence: But if it were my son, I would still be bothered if his partner’s parents thought it was only natural.
p_be39c95a7f.prev: He took his wife’s last name without discussing it with his parents, and I know that his mother, my aunt, was so shocked that she became ill.
p_be39c95a7f.next: I want them to feel at least a little grateful to my son.
